key_insight: SAM2’s object-level representations encode tumour-discriminative information, offering an alternative to conventional encoder-based features.
clinical_relevance: These representations could support imaging-based cancer-type and recurrence prediction, but the study does not establish clinical utility or address drug discovery directly.
method: Extract compact object pointers produced during SAM2 segmentation.
Add an auxiliary prediction objective to create task-guided object pointers.
Compare downstream prediction with encoder-based features and radiomics.
evidence_signal: Across two PET/CT tumour prediction tasks, task-guided pointers improved cancer-type classification over encoder-based transfer and radiomics, while segmentation-only pointers performed best for recurrence prediction.
watch_item: The abstract provides no sample sizes, effect sizes, or external-validation details, limiting assessment of robustness and generalisability.
paper_title: Beyond the Encoder: Object-Centric Representations Emerging from Segmentation Foundation Models
